messages.subject: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
messages.subject_clean: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,
While I am still studying how to apply SECR to determine density and population of Cricetomys rats in an African forest, I am also wondering if it can be used to give me an estimate of "home range". It will really be helpful in my studies. Please does anyone have an idea of a paper I can look at or how to help refine my search.
I will appreciate your swift response.
Biplang

messages.subject: Re: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
messages.subject_clean: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yadok

SECR gives you an estimate of the spatial scale of detection (sigma). This is MUCH better than some conventional trap-revealed measures of home range size (mean maximum distance moved MMDM, asymptotic range length ARL etc.) because it adjusts for the truncation of some ranges at the edge of your trapping grid, and for sample size, BUT it is not the same thing as home range size because it depends on the willingness of animals to enter traps. I came across this nice quote a few weeks ago from Hayne (1949) (J. Mamm. 30: 1–18): “Even if  the  probability  associated  with  the  independent  action  of  a  single  trap  could  be  estimated,  this  would  be  an  index  of  trap-frequenting  activity,  and  not  of  normal  activity.  To  consider  one  type  of  activity  as  directly  reflecting  the  other  is  only  one  possible  explanation.”   SECR takes care of the first issue (action of a single trap) but not the second. SECR also usually (but not necessarily) fits a circular (radially symmetrical) model.

Murray

messages.body_plain:
Hi Biplang

'sigma' is a parameter in the SECR model. It is not fixed - it takes different values in different studies, and may vary within a population according to sex, time etc.

Please note that R is case-sensitive, and there is no package 'SECR'. SECR refers to a set of methods in general.

Murray

messages.subject: cluster.counts error, mask, binary.usage and general organizational questions
messages.subject_clean: cluster.counts error, mask, binary.usage and general organizational questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi All -

I have a small mammal dataset that includes several trapping sessions over several grids. We trapped for 3 years -> 2 separate trapping sessions per year -> 3 nights of trapping per session (6 total sessions, 18 total occasions, at each grid). We have 18 rectangular trapping grids, with 64 pairs of detectors at each grid. The grids are independent from each other - they are located far enough away that we do not detect the same individuals at multiple grids. We have many spatial habitat-related covariates for each detector.

My overall goal is to be able to describe the relationship between density and the habitat covariates. The habitat is quite heterogeneous throughout the study area and even within several of the grids. I'm hoping to run models that have habitat covariates on g0 (detector-level) and D (with the mask covariates), and use both the coefficients from the covariates as well as to make a density surface object to get detector-level (via the mask points) information about how density varies throughout our study area.

Here are the first few lines of my data files and then the script....

Trap data:

Capture data:

Script:

> pkmdets <- read.traps(file="AllDets_TestSpCovs.txt", detector="multi", covnames=c("Gd","Trp","S_Snd","S_Crs","M_TCaps"))
> cdtmask <- make.mask(pkmdets, type="trapbuffer", buffer=40)
> clusterID(pkmdets) <- covariates(pkmdets)$Gd
> clustertrap(pkmdets) <- covariates(pkmdets)$Trp
> pkmCHdata <- read.table("AllGridsPKM.txt", header=TRUE)
> pkmCH <- make.capthist(pkmCHdata, pkmdets, fmt="trapID")
> summary(pkmCH, terse = T)
              1    2    3    4    5    6
Occasions     3    3    3    3    3    3
Detections   99   39  149  393  245  430
Animals      64   29  121  222  139  228
Detectors  1152 1152 1152 1152 1152 1152
> pkm.covs.test <- secr.fit (pkmCH , model = list(D~1,g0~1, sigma~1), start =
+ list(D=20, g0=0.05, sigma=10), verify = FALSE)
Preparing detection design matrices
Preparing density design matrix
Maximizing likelihood...
Eval     Loglik        D       g0    sigma
   1         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3026
   2         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3026
   3         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3026
   4         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3026
   5         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3026
   6         NA   2.9960  -2.9444   2.3026
   7         NA   2.9957  -2.9443   2.3026
   8         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3028
   9         NA   2.9963  -2.9444   2.3026
  10         NA   2.9960  -2.9443   2.3026
  11         NA   2.9960  -2.9444   2.3028
  12         NA   2.9957  -2.9442   2.3026
  13         NA   2.9957  -2.9443   2.3028
  14         NA   2.9957  -2.9444   2.3030
Completed in 61.25 seconds at 16:49:34 22 Mar 2015
Warning message:
In secr.fit(pkmCH, model = list(D ~ 1, g0 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1), start = list(D = 20,  :
  using default buffer width 100 m

When I run basic models, it does not give me errors, and will begin to (try to) estimate, but quickly finishes, listing all LL values as "NA."

In trying to troubleshoot, I've found these things that I believe are issues, but unsure how to fix them.

When I look at the make.capthist object, I get this:

> pkmCH
Session =  1
       1    2    3
102   74   75   75
104   65   65    0
105   66   66   66
106   78    0    0
108   38    0    0
111    0  118  102
113    0   53    0
114    0   50    0
125    0  135    0
126    0  141    0
129    0  160    0
 (this is just the first few lines...)
The first column above makes sense as the eartag number of each individual, but the numbers in the table for each occasion do not make sense to me (they are not detector number/IDs, or counts).

However, when I call this, it makes more sense.
> summary(pkmCH, terse = T)
              1    2    3    4    5    6
Occasions     3    3    3    3    3    3
Detections   99   39  149  393  245  430
Animals      64   29  121  222  139  228
Detectors  1152 1152 1152 1152 1152 1152

Additionally, the clusterID seems to makes sense, but I get errors when trying to look at the cluster.count() fn.
> table(clusterID(pkmdets))

 A  B  C  D  E  F  G  H  I  J  K  L  M  N  O  P  Q  R
64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64
> cluster.counts(pkmCH)
Error in clust[trap(object, names = FALSE)] :
  invalid subscript type 'list'

####
Questions:

1) I'm unsure on where things have gone wrong and how to troubleshoot further with the LL NA's/capt.hist summary/cluster.counts issue. I'm unsure if I'm just not understanding what the CH table is supposed to be summarizing or if there is something wrong in the capture history input file or script. I have seen your suggestions about separating session by grid, however, when I've reorganized the CH input file in that way, it seems that I don't have enough data in each of the subsets to run models. I've also thought about organizing the CH data input so that each grid is a session and then there are 18 occasions per session. But this didn't seem to be appropriate to me since I'm dealing with small mammals, and the density varies significantly during different parts of the year, from year to year, and there are very few individuals that we have caught from one year to the next - but I admit that I don't understand fully how secr would deal with that variation between sessions.

2) Regarding masks - I only have habitat/spatial data at each our our detector locations and not beyond or between grids. Does the make.mask function automatically fill in the mask points in the buffer (when using type="trapbuffer") with the values from the nearest detector covariates? Do I need extra script beyond what I have listed above to do this? I know this would be fairly ad-hoc, but should be a better estimate than

3) Regarding binary.usage - 2 of my 18 grids were not trapped the first year (i.e., the first 2 sessions). I tried to include a column in the trap input file (located after the UTMs and before the / and covariate columns) that had a string of 18 0's and 1's to reflect that those 2 grids were 0's for the first 6 occasions and the rest of the grids and occasions all had 1's. I then also added the binary.usage=TRUE argument to my traps object. However, when I tried to run a model with that data and argument, they would not run due to memory limits errors, regardless of the size of my computer. Are there any other suggestions of how I could organize or specify usage without dropping those 2 grids or sessions?

4) It seems that the cluster functions would be very applicable to my trapping layout/design, and I've included them in my script because I was thinking it would be better to specify "groups" of traps. I have a hunch that this is where my problem lies - that secr is trying to produce estimates for the area between the grids, and since there is no data there (nor do I need that info), it is having trouble doing that. Any other suggestions on how to better organize or specify the data inputs or script would also be welcome.

Many thanks for your thoughts and time.

Sarah

messages.subject: Re: cluster.counts error, mask, binary.usage and general organizational questions
messages.subject_clean: cluster.counts error, mask, binary.usage and general organizational questions
messages.body_plain:
Sarah

Your example is large and complicated by 'secr' standards. I think most of what you want can be achieved by treating each grid x time sample as a session (I make that 108 sessions). You start with 6 sessions (times), in each of which 1152 sites were trapped; the 1152 sites break down into 18 grids. After some trial and error, I got this arcane R code to split the data into a separate 'session' for each of the 108 time x grid combinations

grid <- lapply(covariates(traps(pkmCH)), '[[', 'Gd')  ## trap covariate Gd identifies grids
CH <- mapply(split, pkmCH, grid, bytrap = TRUE, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
CH <- unlist(CH, recursive = FALSE)
class(CH) <- c('list', 'capthist')  ## restore class of collapsed list of capthist objects
## CH is now a 108-session capthist object

I am sceptical about the value of modelling density surfaces within grids (conceptually nice, but each is fairly small and in my experience a lot of data are needed to tie down continuous variation in density, plus you do not have habitat covariates from the zone around the traps). You can instead characterize the overall habitat of each grid on one or more covariates and use those as session-level covariates (provided as a dataframe in the argument 'sessioncov' of secr.fit). You could later project that between-grid covariate model across the landscape between grids (and think about how to justify that extrapolation!)

It turns out in your case that clustering and 'mash' is not going to help, because you don't want to lose the grid-specific covariates.

I couldn't put my finger on why your likelihood would not evaluate at the initial values, but it surely a bad sign.

I noticed that the mask you generated was very coarse once you zoomed in to the vicinity of a particular grid. This is always something to be wary of in a layout with disjunct clusters. The solution is to specify the mask spacing directly in make.mask(), or to split the detector layout into separate grids without dead space between them (as in my multi-session solution).

I hope this is a step forwards!
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Error in extracting mode
messages.body_plain:
Don't set SPDF = TRUE unless you want a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame. A SpatialPolygonsDataFrame has no 'mode' component for you to extract.

Further gratuitous advice: only use fxi.contour if you are really sure you know what it does, and that's what you want!

Murray
